paper_title: An Unfused-Core-Based Nonfullerene Acceptor Enables High-Efficiency Organic Solar Cells with Excellent Morphological Stability at High Temperatures
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2017 - Li - An Unfused‐Core‐Based Nonfullerene Acceptor Enables High‐Efficiency Organic Solar Cells/auto/Advanced Materials - 2017 - Li - An Unfused‐Core‐Based Nonfullerene Acceptor Enables High‐Efficiency Organic Solar Cells.md

knowledge_points.content: DF-PCIC is designed with an unfused-ring core consisting of two cyclopentadithiophene (CPDT) moieties connected to a central 2,5-difluorobenzene (DFB) group, terminated with 2-(3-oxo-2,3-dihydroinden-1-ylidene)malononitrile (IC) groups.
knowledge_points.evidence: DF-PCIC is synthesized with an unfused-ring core containing two cyclopentadithiophene (CPDT) moieties and one 2,5-difluorobenzene (DFB) group... which owns the same A terminal groups (2-(3-oxo-2,3-dihydroinden-1-ylidene) malononitrile, IC) as ITIC.

knowledge_points.content: Intramolecular F...H noncovalent interactions between the fluorine atoms on the benzene ring and the hydrogen atoms on the adjacent CPDT units lock the DF-PCIC molecule into a nearly planar geometry with a dihedral angle of approximately 5.15°.
knowledge_points.evidence: The fluorine atoms on 2,5-difluorobenzene facilitates the F...H noncovalent interaction with the hydrogen atoms on adjacent CPDT units, therefore locking the molecular conformation with a planar geometry... the dihedral angle between the 2,5-difluorobenzene and CPDT units is found to be around 5.15°.

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cells based on the PBDB-T:DF-PCIC blend achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.14%, with an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.91 V, a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 15.66 mA cm⁻², and a fill factor (FF) of 0.72.
knowledge_points.evidence: Thus, we achieve the highest PCE of 10.14% with a Voc of 0.91 V, a Jsc of 15.66 mA cm−2, and an FF of 0.72, under the condition of 0.5% CN additive and 130 °C annealing temperature.

knowledge_points.content: PBDB-T:DF-PCIC devices demonstrate exceptional thermal stability, retaining 69.8% of their initial PCE after 12 hours of thermal treatment at 180 °C, significantly outperforming PBDB-T:PC71BM and PBDB-T:ITIC based devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: Even the temperature is increased to 180 °C, 69.8% initial efficiency can still be kept after 12 h thermal treatment... the devices based on PBDB-T:ITIC are defeated by PBDB-T:DF-PCIC-based ones in device stability.

knowledge_points.content: DF-PCIC exhibits a deep HOMO level of -5.49 eV and a LUMO level of -3.77 eV, with an optical bandgap of 1.59 eV determined from a film absorption onset of 781 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: LUMO and HOMO are calculated as -3.77 and -5.49 eV... the optical bandgap is calculated to be 1.59 eV... from the film absorption onset at around 781 nm.

knowledge_points.content: The optimal processing conditions for the PBDB-T:DF-PCIC active layer involve a donor:acceptor weight ratio of 1:1.2, the use of 0.5% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) as a solvent additive, and thermal annealing at 130 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: The best device performance is reached when 130 °C annealing temperature is applied... 0.5% CN additive... 1:1.2 of D/A weight ratio is the best composition.

knowledge_points.content: Grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXD) analysis shows that thermal annealing at 180 °C dramatically increases the crystal coherence length (CCL) of DF-PCIC π-π stacking in the blend from 14.6 Å to 58.7 Å.
knowledge_points.evidence: The CCL of π-π stacking in out-of-plane direction is estimated to be 58.7 Å, which is much larger than that in the neat film (14.6 Å).

knowledge_points.content: Thermal annealing at 180 °C significantly enhances charge transport in PBDB-T:DF-PCIC films, increasing hole mobility to 1.10 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and electron mobility to 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: The hole mobility is improved from 0.15 × 10⁻⁴ (the as-cast device) to 1.10 × 10⁻⁴ cm2 V⁻¹ s⁻¹ while the electron mobility is improved from 0.10 × 10⁻⁴ (the as-cast device) to 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ cm2 V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

knowledge_points.content: The high thermal stability of DF-PCIC is attributed to the disruption of F...H noncovalent interactions at high temperatures, which causes the molecule to adopt a twisted geometry that prevents the formation of large, performance-degrading aggregates.
knowledge_points.evidence: F...H noncovalent interactions... would be destroyed under thermal treatment at high temperatures... DF-PCIC may adopt a twisted molecular geometry, and thus over aggregation might be avoided at high temperatures.

knowledge_points.content: The existence of F...H noncovalent interactions in DF-PCIC was experimentally verified using temperature-dependent NMR, showing significant chemical shifts in both ¹H and ¹⁹F spectra when heated from room temperature to 100–120 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: To experimentally prove the existence of hydrogen bonds, we compare 1H NMR spectra of DF-PCIC at 120 °C and room temperature... and 19F NMR spectra... at 100 °C and room temperature. The results show that a large shift... happens... indicating that there indeed exist F...H noncovalent interaction.

knowledge_points.content: The study utilized an inverted device architecture consisting of ITO/ZnO/PFN/Active Layer/MoO3/Ag, where PFN acts as an interlayer to improve interface contact.
knowledge_points.evidence: An inverted device structure of indium tin oxide (ITO)/ZnO/poly[9,9-bis(3′-(N,N-dimethylamino)propyl)-2,7-fluorene)- alt-2,7-(9,9-ioctylfluorene](PFN)/PBDB-T:DF-PCIC/MoO3/Ag is adopted.
